executed_reference.provider_model: separate SQLite provider simulator with stable evaluation IDs, same-key idempotency, and reconcile-by-evaluation-ID
executed_reference.controller_model: SQLite WAL with synchronous=FULL for attempt, evaluation intent/outcome, forecast snapshot, switch decision, and incumbent history

ordering_contract: Persist stable attempt identity and baseline restore pointer before evaluation work.
Persist evaluation intent before provider execution.
Persist completed outcome before allowing it to update the best-safe incumbent.
Persist forecast snapshot before it can authorize a switch.
Persist switch decision before alternative evaluation dispatch.
On restart, if local outcome is absent for an existing intent, reconcile the provider by the same stable evaluation identity before any replay.
Only a completed immutable evaluation outcome may advance the incumbent restore pointer.

observed_result.post_provider_effect_crash_recovery: alternative effect was recovered by reconcile; no second execute call occurred

bounded_inference: For the tested local durable-controller plus idempotent/reconcilable-provider model, persisting forecast/switch authority before alternative dispatch and reconciling by stable evaluation identity prevents duplicate completed evaluation effects across these four hard-exit boundaries while preserving a usable safe incumbent restore pointer.
scope_limit: This does not prove exactly-once behavior for arbitrary remote providers, filesystems, network partitions, or providers without durable idempotency/reconciliation. It also does not validate the statistical quality of the forecast itself.
